source.title: Look But Don't Touch with Sparse Autoencoders for Unlearning in Diffusion Models
source.authors: E. Cassano; Riccardo Renzulli; Rayyan Ahmed; Marco Grangetto; S. Alaniz

record.file_problem: The full paper and appendix are present; no apparent truncation or garbling.
record.tranche_reason: The study uses SAE latents as interpretable concept detectors and intervention points, but its own experiments concern concept erasure in diffusion models. It does not measure neuron job shares, explanations' predictive accuracy, or attribution-graph sufficiency as named in the claim versions.
record.gate_note: The paper evaluates SAE-based concept detection, latent steering, and patch replacement for diffusion-model unlearning. Its reported outcomes concern those SAE methods, not the claim versions' neuron-job audit or explanation tests. No results cited from other work are recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The study uses SAE latents (not a model's own neurons) as concept detectors and intervention points for concept erasure in diffusion models. It reports its own unlearning method's performance against multiplier-based SAE steering. It does not measure neuron job shares (V1, V2), revisit the InceptionV1 cat-car neuron (V3), estimate interpretable-neuron shares by architecture or tool (V4), build neuron attribution graphs (V5), or score neuron explanations by activation prediction (V6, V7).
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. SAE latents reliably detect and localize concepts in diffusion models. Multiplier-based steering of those latents produces out-of-distribution activations and artifacts. Using SAEs only for detection, combined with patch embedding replacement, reduces artifacts and improves UnlearnCanvas, NSFW and adversarial results without tuning intervention strength.
record.recipe_differences: The study evaluates SAE-based concept detection, steering, and patch replacement for diffusion-model unlearning; it does not conduct the Qwen neuron-pole audit or test explanation fidelity as described in the claim versions.
record.method_sensitivity: Results vary across SAE pipelines and models; multiplier strength affects activation distributions; PER outcomes vary with padding (p = 0, 1, 2), with the paper identifying p = 1 as a reliable default.

fits_no_version.finding: SAE latents localize target object concepts in diffusion model feature maps precisely (qualitative, Fig. 7). Steering those latents with negative multipliers pushes activations out of distribution and causes artifacts (R1–R8; AR 43–61% vs 1–2% unmodified).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In diffusion models, SAE latents that detect a concept well are not reliable intervention points: steering them produces out-of-distribution activations and visual artifacts.

record.problems: The experiments concern diffusion-model concept erasure, not the claim versions' neuron-job shares, explanation predictive accuracy, or attribution graphs. The main benchmark uses Stable Diffusion v1.5; SDXL Turbo is also tested, but it was not fine-tuned on UnlearnCanvas. Artifact rates are evaluated with Qwen2-VL-7B-Instruct, with a human evaluation on a subset.
record.rows_left_out: No additional results omitted from the recorded rows that directly bear on SAE detection or intervention outcomes. Other reported measures include retention scores, adversarial-attack results, NSFW removal counts, padding ablations, and human preference results; these concern downstream unlearning performance rather than the listed claim versions.

untested.parts: No audit of neuron-pole job shares in Qwen3-32B.
No job-share measurement across language models, dense or MoE, or across scale.
No analysis of InceptionV1 cat-car or other canonical polysemantic neurons.
No measurement of the share of interpretable neurons by architecture, regularization or tool quality. The paper only asserts polysemanticity as background.
No attribution graphs and no circuit analysis with native neurons.
No test of whether explanations from activating examples predict firing. SAE latent localization is shown only qualitatively (Fig. 7), for SAE latents rather than neurons.
No simulation-based scoring of neuron explanations.

record.verdict_notes: This is a diffusion-model unlearning paper about SAE latents, not native neurons. It mentions polysemanticity only as background, citing Bricken et al. It is not a test of any version. The detection-versus-steering gap is loosely related to V6's theme that interpretation by inspection need not imply control, but V6 concerns predicting firing, which is not measured here. The record's 'partial' states on R13–R16 are not meaningful against any version. The paper's text is internally inconsistent on SDXL Turbo: it gives 83.7% of values outside the distribution but also says 'half activations'.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not audit the share of neuron poles with one or multiple jobs, or the share not understood, in Qwen3-32B or another model.
The study does not measure job shares across language models, model sizes, dense models, or mixture-of-experts.
The study does not analyze InceptionV1's cat-and-car neuron or test recursive generalization against superposition.
The study does not test whether architecture, regularization, or tools explain interpretability rates, or estimate those rates for InceptionV1-sized vision models.
The study does not build attribution graphs or test whether a model's own neurons explain behavior without a trained replacement model.
The study does not test explanations against activations from examples they were not written from, or compare explanation fit to prediction of firing.
The study does not score neuron explanations by simulating activations on new text or report the share of neurons with good scores.
